scenes.text: An AI tutor that won't give answers. Stuck on a maths problem at 11 PM, you ask an AI tutor, and instead of just giving the answer, it asks you a question back. [1] So how do AI tutor apps actually teach? [2] Let's break it down.

data.subtitle: How AI teaches you
data.hook: An AI tutor that *won't give answers*

scenes.text: Here's what happens when you ask for help. [1] You upload your homework question. [2] The tutor reads your textbook chapter, using RAG, so it teaches your syllabus. [3] It checks its memory of you, like what you struggled with last week. [4] It gives you a hint, not the answer, and asks you to try the next step, [5] and it adapts, based on how you respond.

data.heading: When you ask for help
nodes: A photo of a maths problem
Not the answer, the next step
Harder or easier, based on you

scenes.text: And the magic is mostly in the instructions. [1] A plain assistant just gives the answer, x equals 4. [2] A tutor gets a role, you are a patient maths tutor for a class 9 student. [3] A rule, never give the final answer directly. [4] A method, give one hint at a time, and ask a question back. [5] And a format, short, friendly and encouraging. [6] Now it guides you to the answer yourself.

data.heading: The tutor's instructions

data.goodReply: Great start! What could you subtract from both sides to get 2x on its own?

scenes.text: So what makes a good AI tutor? [1] Socratic questions, guiding you with questions, instead of answers. [2] Adaptive difficulty, harder when you're doing well, easier when you're stuck. [3] Spaced practice, bringing back old topics before you forget them. [4] And encouragement, because confidence matters.
Here's the big difference. [1] An answer bot gives you the answer, and you learn nothing. [2] A good tutor makes you think, so you can solve the next problem on your own.

right.title: AI tutor
right.label: you solve the next one alone

scenes.text: So where will you see this? [1] Learning apps with AI tutors for school maths and science. [2] Language apps that chat with you, and correct your mistakes. [3] And coding platforms that give hints when your code fails.

Here's a common myth. [1] People think AI tutors will replace teachers. [2] They're great for practice at any hour, but teachers bring motivation, judgement, and understanding each student as a person. The best results come from both together.

data.fact: Great for practice any time, but teachers bring motivation, judgement and care. Both together work best.
